item.title: Tecnologo: Development of new systems for measuring and certifying agricultural sprayers with a view to mitigating the drift of plant protection products (Extension of the Prog.iNEST-Spoke1 project – Research Topic 1B) (Univ. BOLZANO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-09 12:00
Institution: Univ. BOLZANO, Bolzano
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-04 Ingegneria agraria, forestale e dei biosistemi

Support in the development of measurement systems for assessing the distribution dynamics of plant protection products using orchard sprayers, in accordance with mass balance approaches. The new systems will integrate direct measurement activities using flow interception devices (vertical and horizontal patternators) with modelling approaches, with the aim of estimating the fractions destined to: 1) effectively reach the canopy (target); 2) settling on the ground; 3) remaining in aerial suspension in the form of an aerosol. Research support activities will take place at the ‘Agroforestry Innovation Laboratory (AFI-Lab)’ of the Free University of Bolzano, located at the NOI Techpark South…

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-04 12:00
Institution: Univ. BOLZANO, Bolzano
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-08 Microbiologia agraria, alimentare e ambientale

Support for innovative fermentation processes aimed at valorizing and recycling food by-products, using alternative raw materials, and developing products and processes with high nutritional value. item.title: Tecnologo: NEXT-G FIS-2023-02552 CUP I53C24003120001 “How new genes emerge: exploring a model of novel gene creation following the evolution of wheat” (Univ. PISA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-09 13:00
Institution: Univ. PISA, Pisa
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-06 Genetica, chimica e pedologia agraria e forestale

The NEXT-G project explores how transposons, DNA elements capable of rapidly reorganizing genomes, contribute to the creation of new genes in wheat through the process of exaptation. By applying bioinformatic and genomic approaches, it investigates the evolutionary impact of transposons on the creation of new genes and the mechanisms that drive this process. Focusing on wheat, the project offers new perspectives on the evolution of plant genomes and on adaptation to selective pressures, with particular attention to the early stages of domestication.
